Judgment

01. The petitioner has challenged the legality, propriety and correctness of impugned detention order No. 43/DMP/PSA/23, dated 26.06.2023, read with the Govt. Order no. Home/ PB-V/1553 of 2023 dated 03.07.2023 passed by the District Magistrate, Pulwama under J&K Public Safety Act,
whereof the preventive detention of the petitioner has been ordered so as to prevent him from acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
The petitioner has assailed this order of detention through his father-Fazal Din Malik.

02. The grounds of detention reveal that the SSP, Awantipora submitted a dossier to the District Magistrate of Pulwama, reporting that the petitioner, along with accomplices namely: (i) Umer Nazir Rather, son of Nazir Ahmad Rather, resident of Shikargah Tral, (ii) Dr. Asim Afzal Mir, son of Mohd. Afzal Mir, resident of Bandipora, (iii) Shahnawaz Ahmad Khan, son of Mohammad Amin Mohd. Abid Malik vs (I) Union Territory Of J&K on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173107270/
1 Khan, resident of Sumbal Sonawari, (iv) Yawar Ahmad Naikoo, son of Gh. Qadir Naikoo, resident of Kiloora Shopian, and (v) Shabir Ahmad Wani, son of Abdul Hamid Wani, resident of Soibugh Budam, were luring students and their families into illegally providing them with fake question papers for the B.Sc. Nursing exams.

These exams were conducted by the J&K BOPEE on 11.06.2023,
and the individuals were arrested by the police for extorting large sums of money for this illegal act.

03. The grounds of detention further reveal that the petitioner was attempting to lure students and parents into providing question papers for various examinations with the aid of artificial intelligence technology, facilitating the rapid dissemination of such papers among interested examinees, thereby earning substantial amounts of money.

This activity jeopardizes the careers of thousands of brilliant young students, erodes the trust and credibility of government institutions, and creates a strong sense of resentment and hatred against the government, with the potential to incite protests and disturb the peace.

The petitioner had established a nexus with other criminal elements that are adept at entrapping students under the pretense of providing question papers for every examination conducted at the state or central level in exchange for substantial consideration.

The petitioner, for the aforementioned acts, was booked under FIR No. 53/2023 for commission of offences under Sections 420 and 120-B of IPC at Police Station, Tral.
04.

It is further stated in the dossier that the activities of the petitioner were deemed highly prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, demonstrating a strong motivation to pursue illegal designs.

The petitioner was unlikely to refrain from undesirable activities that threaten public order,
and normal laws were insufficient to deter him from engaging in such actions, resultantly, the District Magistrate, Pulwama, passed the detention order No. 43/DMP/PSA/23, dated 26.06.2023.
05.

The petitioner has assailed the order of detention on number of grounds, i.e., (i) the impugned detention order issued by respondent No. 2 on 26.06.2023 states that the petitioner's activities are prejudicial to public order, necessitating immediate detention, however, the allegations considered prejudicial do not fall under the activities defined as such in Section 8(3)(b) of the Act, indicating total non-application of mind; (ii) the grounds of detention, can only be interpreted as an apprehension of a breach of law and order, and do not constitute an apprehension of a breach of public order.

FIR No. 53/2023 has been cited as the sole basis for the detention order, and it does not contain any allegations of sufficient magnitude to create a breach of public order; (iii) the petitioner is a permanent resident of Jammu and is a government employee working as an Assistant Veterinary Surgeon in Jammu and he has no connection with District Pulwama, thus, it is unreasonable to view him as a person whose antecedents are prejudicial to public order in that district; (iv) The impugned order was passed only on the basis of dossier submitted by SSP,
Awantipora;

(v) respondent No. 2 has failed to arrive at a subjective satisfaction as to how the alleged activities of the petitioner are detrimental and prejudicial to public order; (vi) the detention order alleges that the petitioner has created a law-and-order problem and the petitioner cannot be detained under law-and-order issue; (vii) There is total non- application of mind as the circulation of news regarding exam leakage in media, the government issued a press release on 13.06.2023 denying the allegations of paper leakage.
The examination was conducted as scheduled on 11.06.2023, and the results have already been declared.
This fact has not been considered by the respondents.

sentences.text: The petitioner along with others was arrested on 10.06.2023 in FIR No. 53/2023 and on 12.06.2023, the petitioner filed an application under section 437 Cr.P.C. before the Court of the learned Munsiff, Tral, seeking regular bail, which was granted as interim bail on 16.06.2023 and has been extended until today.

During the bail hearing, the Investigating Officer and the prosecuting agency reported nothing adverse against the accused, and these findings were recorded by the Ld.
Munsiff in the bail extension order dated 26.06.2023.
07.

It is further submitted that respondent no. 2 exercised his powers under the J&K Public Safety Act, 1978, in an unreasonable, unjustified, arbitrary, and mala fide manner, infringing upon the petitioner's personal liberty, as such, the petitioner has approached this Court seeking setting aside of the impugned detention order.
08. Mrs. Monika Kohli, learned Sr. AAG, has filed the counter affidavit as well as produced the relevant record.
09. It is submitted by the respondents that the activities of the petitioner have been found prejudicial to the security of the State.
The police recommended his preventive detention and submitted a dossier supported by relevant material to the District Magistrate.

After examining the record and material, and finding the preventive detention of the petitioner necessary, the order was passed with the sole aim of deterring the petitioner from acting in any manner that is prejudicial to the security of the State.
10. The respondents have further stated that the grounds on which the detention order has been passed are unequivocally substantiated and justified.
The interim order of the Court whereby the detention order is stayed, has incapacitated the respondents from proceeding further in the matter and has resulted in stagnation.

11. A perusal of the grounds of detention would draw out that for alleged involvement of the petitioner in an alleged racket of providing fake question papers of BSc Nursing Exams conducted by the J&K Board of Profession Entrance Examinations, the petitioner came to be booked under FIR no. 53/2023 under section 420 read with section 120-B of IPC of Police Station, Tral.

entities.text: J&K Board of Profession Entrance Examinations
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
12. The activities of the petitioner at the best even if taken at its face value to be correct, are a part of law-and-order problem but surely not falling within the domain of maintenance of public order and as such the preventive detention of the petitioner on this premise is misconceived and unwarranted.
13.
This Court has already considered the detention of Yawar Ahmad Naikoo and Umar Nazir Rather in HCP No. 47/2023 and HCP No. 45/2023, respectively, based on a similar FIR, which has been quashed.
Therefore, this Court finds that no different conclusion can be reached in the present case as well.

14. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of this case, this Court holds that the preventive detention of the petitioner was misconceived given the fact that the alleged acts of omission and commission on the part of the petitioner allegedly acting in complicity with the aforementioned Mohd. 3 persons resulting in his implication in FIR No. 53/2023 of the Police Station Tral in no manner can be construed to be prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
15.

sentences.text: The impugned preventive detention order No. 43/DMP/PSA/23, dated 26.06.2023, passed by the respondent No. 2 - District Magistrate, Pulwama, is, accordingly, quashed.
16. Record be returned to the learned counsel for the respondents by the Registry forthwith.
